intelligence.human_view: The mistake would have been to polish the endless-links My World — to make the confusing thing prettier and call it done. Shawn's ruling kills that path: the shape itself goes away when the calendar is built, so this round redesigns only the picker — the doorway — and refuses to entrench what the calendar will replace. The same discipline applies to the news feeds: they are not worlds to feature; they live ON THE DAY, with a beautiful toggle, off by default. And the word matters: "thing", not "space" — your world, your space, your thing — because the citizen's language is the system's language. The round's delivery was honest about the boundary: the picker is done, the calendar is not, and the calendar is the build that follows.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you have a big messy drawer full of tangled strings, and someone says "let's make the drawer prettier!" But the real answer is: you don't need that drawer at all — you need a beautiful calendar, where every day is a little box and everything for that day lives inside it. So you fix the little door that opens the drawer, and you save the big beautiful calendar for next — you don't build a prettier mess!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — if the cupboard is a jumble, you don't polish the jumble. You fix the little handle so it opens nicely, and you build the proper shelves next — a calendar, where every day holds everything for that day, neat and easy. And the news? It lives on the day it happened, not in the cupboard. Simple as that.
intelligence.naya_view: My World IS the calendar. Redesign the picker, don't entrench the endless links. News feeds live ON THE DAY, off by default. The word is "thing".
